ranking.note: Confirmed-exploitable control-port injection/onion hijack is the strongest security item after #36015, so it leads the P2 band.
Abort/out-of-bounds write on outbound encoding is a crash-class defect, same tier as #35919, so it moves up with it.
Indefinite IBD headers stall is a liveness failure with a reproducer; ranked above the privacy/feature P2s.
Light clients banning Core nodes is an interoperability regression with other implementations waiting, which this category ranks above local features.
Closes an inbound relay-capacity accounting bypass; attack-resistance items lead the band per category priorities.
False terrible-marking of remote addresses degrades addrman/gossip for multi-network nodes; grouped with the other addrman/relay correctness P2s.
Category-defining bandwidth/eclipse work, but the author intends to carve it into reviewable PRs, so concrete fixes with certain benefit come first.
Opt-in encryption policy feature; ranked below the concrete correctness and DoS fixes in the same band.
Placed at the head of the private-broadcast cluster (broadest coverage) rather than among the top P2 fixes.
Overlaps #34457 on rebroadcast privacy; kept adjacent to it instead of near the top of the band.
Problem (onboarding without third-party snapshots) stays P2, but concept opposition and an unresolved architectural dispute make the benefit least certain in the band.
Raised from P4 and placed at the top of P3: it is the stacked prerequisite for #35558 and inherits some of its importance.
Silent stuck chain / assertion abort on block-read failure is the most consequential remaining P3.
Grouped with #35888 as message-limit hardening; DoS-evasion fixes lead the P3 band per category priorities.
Kept P3 but ranked first among the refactors since it retires a known recursive-locking hazard in message handling (#19303).
Protocol-compliance fix in INV handling with disconnect behavior; ranked with the other relay-correctness P3s.
Consistent misbehavior scoring on the compact-block fallback path belongs with the other relay-correctness fixes.
Startup failure when following official docs is a user-visible defect, above the internal refactors.
Addrman multiplicity logic bug ranked with the other addrman correctness items rather than near the bottom.
Useful reliability feature for manual/pruned-rescan flows, but narrower than the correctness fixes above it.
Observability alternative to #36277; kept just below it so the design choice is decided first.
Internal refactor with no user-facing effect; grouped with the other net/net_processing decoupling PRs.
Grouped with the other structural refactors, below fixes with user-visible effect.
Type-safety cleanup with only marginal eviction-ordering effect; sits with the refactor group.
Telemetry only, no protocol effect; below the refactors that retire hazards or unblock the split.
Test-only coverage of existing behavior; placed with the other test PRs rather than mid-list.
Mostly an RPC field plus test coverage, so it ranks with the test PRs at the bottom of P3.
Lowered to P4 to match #35522: both are pure move-only decompositions of net_processing with no hazard retired.

inconsistencies: #34457 and #34533 overlap: both route wallet rebroadcasts through private broadcast. #34457 is the superset (sends + rebroadcasts + reachability check), so review it first and treat #34533 as the narrower alternative.
#34707 and #36277 are stated alternatives for the same private-broadcast completion/status problem; #36277 fixes the timing side-channel and should be decided first, #34707 only adds observability.
Chain: #35724 must be reviewed before #35558 (prefill is stacked on the reconstruction-logging split). #35724 was scored P4 on its own but cannot sit below the PR it gates.

Private-broadcast cluster (#34322, #34457, #34533, #34707, #34271, #36277) all extend the feature merged in #29415 and touch the same state; they should be sequenced together rather than reviewed independently, and #34271 depends on the architectural direction the others settle.

#35502 and #35522 are the same kind of work on the same file (move-only extraction from ProcessMessage vs SendMessages) and were given different bands when assessed alone; aligned to P4 and they will conflict with each other and with the refactors #34565/#34824/#35561.

#30988 (SockMan/CConnman split), #35040 (LocalAddressManager), #34565 (BlockDownloadManager), #34824 (TxRelay) are parts of the same net/net_processing decoupling effort (#30694/#33958); #30988 is the broadest and should set the direction before the narrower extractions land.
#35888 (outbound message size limits) and #35936 (inbound oversized locator counts) harden the same class of size-limit gap from opposite directions; reviewing them together is cheaper.
#36267 is by design a backport of work already merged in master (#36256, #36260); its value is release-branch only, not new p2p change.
result.notes: The P2 band is crowded (21 PRs) because this category's attack-resistance, relay-correctness and privacy work genuinely clusters there; ordering inside P2 puts confirmed crash/exploit and measured propagation fixes ahead of feature and refactor work. Several cards' self-assessed positions over-ranked large unmergeable projects (#35591, #35054) and under-ranked interoperability/liveness fixes (#35354, #35839, #35888), which accounts for most of the position shifts.
